solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Support Britain wanting rid of leader

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for Britain, as on car plates

indicators.note: a word with its leader gone has its first letter taken away

parts.note: wanting means lacking, short of something

explanation.surface: A political lament: the country, missing its head, still needs support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rid of leader' takes the first letter off LACKING to leave ACKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: backing given to a cause or person is support for it.

clue.text: Being somewhat less shocked than before?!

definitions.text: Being somewhat less shocked than before?!

parts.words: Being somewhat less shocked than before?!
parts.note: a shock is also a thick mass of hair, so having less of it means thinning on top

explanation.surface: Someone recovering from a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A head of hair thinning so it is partly bare is the state described.

clue.text: Person in the employ of the police artist

definitions.text: Person in the employ of the police
definitions.meaning: a police officer of the lowest rank
John ..., English landscape painter of The Hay Wain

explanation.definitionFit: A British police officer of basic rank, and the English Romantic landscape painter.

clue.text: I bring legal proceedings about small matter

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pieces surround this one

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A litigant suing over something trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a matter under discussion is an issue, a subject or topic.

clue.text: Plant men regard in a state of excitement

indicators.note: letters that are excited are agitated and stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Men getting worked up over a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Germander is a herb or shrub of the mint family, genus Teucrium.

clue.text: Chatter pointlessly on black Blackberry

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencil grades
to ramble is to talk on aimlessly

explanation.surface: Someone babbling idly on a dark-coloured Blackberry phone.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B in 'Blackberry' suggests the phone; the definition is the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The bramble is the wild blackberry bush, and its fruit is also called a bramble.

clue.text: One's to tuck into good French beef alternative

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so this piece is placed within the other

parts.note: bon is French for good
one's read as one is gives I plus S, the numeral I for one

explanation.surface: Someone about to eat a fine French substitute for beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read as 'one is', giving I (Roman one) and S.
explanation.definitionFit: The meat of the American buffalo is eaten as a leaner substitute for steak.

clue.text: Sadly, our old cat is horrible

indicators.note: sadly here means badly or wretchedly, so the letters are arranged poorly and reworked

explanation.surface: A lament that the family's elderly pet is in a terrible state.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something atrocious is appalling, very bad.

clue.text: Pancake day is shunned by visually impaired institute

indicators.note: a letter shunned by a word is avoided by it, so it is taken out

parts.note: blind means without sight

explanation.surface: Pancake Day ignored by an institution for the blind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pancake day' reads as Shrove Tuesday, but 'day' belongs to the wordplay. 'is shunned by' takes D from BLIND to leave BLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Russian buckwheat pancake, often served with sour cream and caviar.

clue.text: Pull out more conservative trunks at the front

parts.note: extra means additional, more

indicators.note: the front of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Pulling out a more modest pair of swimming trunks.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to remove a tooth or draw something out is to pull it out.

clue.text: Punishment for a schoolboy error?

parts.note: the standard school penalty of writing out a sentence many times; the question mark flags the actor's sense of a fluffed script

explanation.surface: A teacher wondering how to punish a pupil's mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing the same sentence over and over is the classic school punishment, and an actor's forgotten words are also the thing in question.

clue.text: Reserve shower possibly during leisure time

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so this piece goes inside

parts.note: leisure is rest, time off
a shower is one example of rain falling

explanation.surface: Someone advises holding back on a shower in your spare time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' suggests bathing, but here it is weather; 'during' places it inside leisure time.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: reserve, as a quality of character, is self-restraint and holding back.

clue.text: A hint men and I must change for the most part

indicators.note: the letters are required to change, so they are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A note that men, and the speaker, must largely change their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: something true generally or mostly holds on the whole, mostly.

clue.text: Church popular with a friend in the East End

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A churchgoer who is well liked, with a pal from London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang, spoken in London's East End, 'china plate' rhymes with mate, shortened to the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang uses this word for a mate, a close pal.

clue.text: Rather put on hot clothes

indicators.note: one piece put on another in an across clue follows it, so these letters come second

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
rather, as in rather cold, means a bit

explanation.surface: Someone choosing to wear warm clothes instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' looks like dressing, but it places A BIT after H.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun's or monk's robe is called by this name, a garment of distinctive dress.

clue.text: Tickle a little drunk with it

indicators.note: drunk letters are unsteady and stagger into another order

explanation.surface: Getting slightly tipsy on it is a pleasant tease.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to stimulate or excite pleasantly, as a light tickle does.

clue.text: Don't adore criminal that smells nice

indicators.note: something criminal is wrong or crooked, so the letters are bent into another order

explanation.surface: A plea not to admire a lawbreaker just because they smell good.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Don't' is ignored; DONTADORE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A product applied to the body to mask odour, leaving a pleasant scent.

clue.text: Old Republican steps, perhaps to secure home rule

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast within, so this piece goes inside

parts.note: dance steps are one example of a dance
in means at home

explanation.surface: An old-school Republican taking measures to ensure home rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home rule' runs together in the surface, but 'home' belongs to the wordplay ('to secure' places it inside the steps) and 'rule' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: an ordinance is an authoritative decree or regulation, especially a local law.

clue.text: Possibly touching description of a hypotenuse?

definitions.text: Possibly touching description of a hypotenuse?

parts.words: Possibly touching description of a hypotenuse?
parts.note: the longest side of a right-angled triangle can be described with a phrase meaning next to

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle about the long edge of a triangle.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the long edge of a triangle; as one word it means next to, possibly in contact.

clue.text: Do back detaining bad riveter in need of the sack

indicators.note: detaining means holding something within, so the second piece goes inside
back means the word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: do here is the word taken letter for letter

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of riveter are spoiled and jumbled

explanation.surface: A weary worker who botched some riveting and deserves to be fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the sack' suggests dismissal, but it is slang for bed. 'back' turns the first word round, and 'detaining' holds the jumbled letters ('bad') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sack is slang for bed, so someone in need of bed is exhausted from too little sleep.

clue.text: Expose men holding party in the open air

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them
a do is a party
OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Exposing men who are throwing a party out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor activities take place outside, under the sky rather than in a building.

clue.text: Philosophical type objects to ice-cream sandwiches

indicators.note: the words sandwich the answer between them, holding it inside

explanation.surface: A thinker who disapproves of ice-cream sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like the dessert but signals the run of letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Stoic school of philosophy, which teaches calm endurance.

clue.text: Dispute examination of a prisoner?

indicators.note: an examination of something names the thing examined, which comes first here

parts.note: a con, short for convict, is a prisoner
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Arguing over the interrogation of an inmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to dispute a claim is to challenge or contest it.

clue.text: Test case?

definitions.meaning: a test or experiment, as in a drug being tried out
a court case heard before a judge

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a try-out to see if something works, and a hearing in court.

clue.text: I do business with another model

parts.note: to deal is to trade with someone

explanation.surface: A boast of trading with another model.
explanation.definitionFit: A model example is a perfect one, a standard to aim for.

clue.text: Successful movement of a tour bus, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a popular cause or trend that people rush to join
a vehicle carrying a musical group, a group's wagon

explanation.surface: Describing a winning campaign by a touring coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping on this means joining a popular trend; split, it is a vehicle for musicians on tour.

clue.text: Endure first part of bachelor party

indicators.note: the first part of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a rave is a wild party

explanation.surface: Getting through the opening stage of a stag party.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to brave hardship is to face and endure it.

clue.text: Undamaged, but unattractive place reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the word that sounds the same is entered

parts.note: a hole is a dingy, unpleasant place

explanation.surface: A place that is intact but grim, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something whole is intact, all in one piece.

clue.text: Romeo Vera gainfully cuddles another time

indicators.note: the words hold the answer close inside them, as in a hug

explanation.surface: Romeo hugs Vera eagerly once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: doing a thing once more, from the start, is doing it a second time.

clue.text: Piece of oily and, on the turn, bad fruit

indicators.note: a piece of a word here is just its first letter
turning round means the word is read backwards

parts.note: bad means wicked, evil

explanation.surface: Some oily fruit that is going off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the turn' (going off, of food) makes LIVE from EVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The small oily stone fruit of the Mediterranean tree, eaten or pressed for oil.

clue.text: Assume responsibility of another's Duty Free

definitions.meaning: take over a post from someone, as a sentry being stood down
set loose, ease of a burden

explanation.definitionFit: One takes over another's shift on watch, and one frees someone from pain or worry.

clue.text: As an example, one might say Krypton Factor

definitions.text: As an example, one might say Krypton
definitions.meaning: krypton is a chemical substance in the periodic table

explanation.definitionFit: Krypton is one of the chemical substances in the periodic table; a factor is a component part.
